display.purpose: The h1 on the home stage. Page heads cap at 64px, docs at 48px.

headline.purpose: The h2 that opens a band.

title.purpose: The heading beside a screenshot in a feature row; walkthrough step titles.

subhead.purpose: h3 in steps and ruled cards, and the heading of a warning card, in Hanken Grotesk 700.

lede.purpose: The paragraph under a display title, max 60ch.

body.purpose: Prose. 16.5px under 900px; 68ch on promo pages, 72ch in docs.

label.purpose: Controls, nav links and small headings. Sentence case, weight 600.

fine.purpose: Fine print, captions, counters, table heads, in Mute; Dim on a page head or the stage, where it sits on a painting.

numeral.purpose: The step number in a row of steps.

shadows.name: deck-front
shadows.purpose: The front window of the deck: a wide soft layer, a close dark layer and the brightest hairline on the site.

shadows.name: deck-back
shadows.purpose: Every window behind the front one on the deck.

shadows.name: window
shadows.purpose: Screenshots in feature rows and the walkthrough; the blade demo at .5 alpha.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The docs search results, with a 1px Strong Line border in place of the ring.

shadows.name: primary-lift
shadows.purpose: Under a primary button, so it reads over a painting.

shadows.name: lettering-title
shadows.purpose: text-shadow on the stage title; smaller stage text uses 0 1px 10px at .7 and 0 1px 8px at .8; the clear top bar's links use 0 1px 8px at .9.

shadows.name: shade-stage
shadows.purpose: Shades over the stage backdrop: at the left for the lettering, at the foot for the theme names, at the head for the top bar.

shadows.name: shade-pagehead
shadows.purpose: Shade over a page head's painting.

shadows.name: shade-scene
shadows.purpose: Shade over the painting behind the closing band.

shadows.name: shade-pagehead-narrow
shadows.purpose: The page head shade under 900px, where the lettering runs the full width.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve: the deck's slide and the button press.

motion.name: deck-slide
motion.purpose: A deck window moving to its new place: translate(calc(var(--i) * 30px), calc(var(--i) * -44px)) scale(calc(1 - var(--i) * .035)). Under 980px the step is 9px, -13px and 3%.

motion.name: deck-focus
motion.purpose: A deck window's softness and brightness following its place: blur(min(2.4px, calc(var(--i) * .45px))) brightness(max(.5, calc(1 - var(--i) * .075))). Hover removes the filter.

motion.name: deck-lift
motion.purpose: The whole deck rises as the page scrolls, where scroll-driven animation is supported; not under 980px.

motion.name: accent-change
motion.purpose: The mark's blade (color) and the stage's hue layer (background-color) changing to a newly chosen accent.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Background, border and transform on controls; .25s for the progress bar; .3s for the home top bar turning solid.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No slide or filter transition on deck windows, no lift, no smooth scrolling.

narrative.overview:
The site is a workshop bay in neutral graphite: a dark, even, colorless room where the app is the thing on show. It has no palette of its own beyond graphite and a cool white. All the color on a page comes from the app: from its ten themes shown as windows, from the theme paintings, and from one accent that the site borrows from whichever theme the visitor has chosen. Choose a theme on the home page and the primary buttons, the blade of the mark and the browser tab icon all take that theme's accent, on every page, until another is chosen.

Density is low on the promo pages (one idea per band, a picture beside most of them) and steady on the reading pages: the walkthrough keeps a painting only behind its page head, and the docs carry none and are a plain three-column reader on the same ground. Everything a visitor can press is a pill. Everything that shows the app is a rounded window with a soft, deep shadow and a hairline edge. The accent fills the primary action and nothing else, amber is kept for caution, and every small mark (underlines, dots, focus rings, progress) is cool white, so a page reads the same whichever theme lends the accent.

The home stage is the system's one piece of theater: a deck of ten app windows, one per theme, the chosen one sharp in front and the rest stepping up and to the right, each smaller, dimmer and softer. Behind the deck is a grayscale painting of a sabersmith's bench in a ship's bay, out of focus, whose one small indicator light takes the accent's hue. Elsewhere the theme paintings appear in two ways: shaded, behind a page head or the closing band, where lettering sits on them; and clear, as a full-bleed band at full strength with no lettering on it, in a tall section.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral graphite ground with three tonal steps (well, raised, high) and cool white lettering; no warm darks.
One accent, borrowed from the chosen theme and remembered across pages; a deep red when scripts are off.
Amber means caution only: the warning card and the warning callout.
Gloock for titles at regular weight, Hanken Grotesk for everything read or pressed.
Pill controls with a 1.5px translucent white edge; the selected state inverts to white.
The app is shown as a floating window, never in a device frame; on the home stage, as a deck of ten.
Paintings are whole surfaces: shaded where lettering sits on them, clear where it does not.
Motion is the deck's slide and a lift on scroll; both stop under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Accent Follows the Theme Rule
rules.body: The site has no accent of its own. It borrows the accent of the theme the visitor chose on the home deck: an inline script in the head of every page sets the accent, its hover and its ink before anything paints, from a table the build makes out of the themes' own accents. The choice is kept in localStorage under hw-theme and holds on every page. Never write an accent value into a rule; use the custom properties (--lamp, --lamp-hi, --lamp-ink), and never assume the accent is red, or light, or dark.

rules.name: The One Accent Fill Rule
rules.body: An accent fill on a control means this is the primary action here. A group of controls carries at most one. Everything else in the group is a clear pill with a white edge.

rules.name: The Marks Are White Rule
rules.body: Anything small that points, counts or tracks is Cel White, not the accent: link underlines, step dots, the focus ring, selection, the current-page and current-chapter highlight, progress and range controls. The accent changes with the theme; the marks must not.

rules.name: The Graphite Rule
rules.body: Every dark is graphite and every light is Cel White. Shades over paintings are the Well color at an alpha, lines are Cel White at an alpha (14% and 32%), and translucent fills on controls are Ground or Well at an alpha. No warm darks, and no tint of any theme in the ground.

rules.name: The Amber Means Caution Rule
rules.body: Amber is not an accent here. It appears only on warning surfaces (the download warning card, the docs warning callout), as an 8% tint with a 60% edge and a Caution Highlight label, and it does not change with the theme. A warning never carries a solid fill. Three themes (The Ninth Jedi, Coruscant at night, Kashyyyk) have amber accents of their own; when one is chosen, the accent is still only a solid fill on a control and caution is still only a tint and an edge.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels, table heads, nav group names and footer column labels are sentence case at weight 600 or 700 with no added tracking. The only uppercase, letter-spaced text on the site is the wordmark in the top bar and footer (700, 0.2em).

rules.name: The One Weight Serif Rule
rules.body: Gloock is always 400. Emphasis in a title comes from size, never from a bolder or italic cut. Headings balance their line breaks (text-wrap: balance).

rules.name: The Shade Before Text Rule
rules.body: Lettering never sits on a painting at full strength. Behind a page head a shade in the Well color runs from 94% at the text side to 35% at the far side; behind the closing band, from 92% to 50%. Under 900px, where lettering runs the full width, both become even shades from top to bottom (78% to 90%, and 80% to 86%). The stage backdrop is already gray and out of focus, so its shades are lighter: 45% at the left falling to clear, 80% at the foot under the theme names, 50% at the head under the top bar, and the lettering carries a soft dark shadow; under 980px it takes one vertical shade (72%, 50%, 80%). A tall section does not put lettering on its painting at all: the painting is a clear band and the rows stand on Graphite Ground below it.

rules.name: The Hairline With Every Shadow Rule
rules.body: A floating window always pairs its soft shadow with a 1px Cel White ring (26% on a window back in the deck, 32% on a screenshot, 36% on the deck's front window). The ring, not the shadow, is what separates a dark screenshot from the dark ground.

rules.name: The One Sharp Window Rule
rules.body: On the deck only the front window is sharp and at full brightness. Each window behind it sits 30px further right and 44px further up, 3.5% smaller, 7.5% dimmer (never below 50%) and 0.45px softer (never above 2.4px). Choosing a theme deals it to the front: its window slides forward over 0.7s on cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) while the windows that stood in front of it each move one step back, and the blur and dimming follow over 0.5s. A window under the pointer comes sharp and bright, so it can be judged before it is chosen. Where scroll-driven animation is supported the whole deck lifts 60px over the first screen of scroll. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the windows change places without the slide and the deck does not lift.

dos: Do take the accent from the custom properties (--lamp, --lamp-hi, --lamp-ink) and let the chosen theme set them; check a new surface with a light accent (Station green, Original cyan) and a dark one (Crait red).
Do keep one accent-filled button per group of controls, with Accent Ink text.
Do draw small marks in Cel White: link underlines (white at 50%), step dots, the focus ring (2px Cel White, 3px offset), selection, progress.
Do keep amber for caution: an 8% tint, a 60% edge and a Caution Highlight label.
Do put a Well-colored shade under any lettering that sits on a painting, heaviest on the text side. In a tall section keep lettering off the painting and show it as a clear band.
Do show the app as a floating window: 10px corners, deep soft shadow, 1px white hairline.
Do make every pressable thing a pill with a 1.5px translucent white edge, and show the selected state by inverting to Cel White with Graphite Ground text.
Do caption a feature picture with the theme it is shown in.
Do set titles in Gloock 400 and everything else in Hanken Grotesk; labels in sentence case at 600.
Do separate flat content with rules (1.5px above a step or card, 1px between bands) and keep it shadowless.
Do give every motion a still state under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
donts: Don't take anything from the chosen theme but its accent. The ground stays graphite, and the shapes and type stay the site's own; the themes otherwise appear only as paintings and as captures inside windows.
Don't write an accent value into a rule, and don't assume the accent is red.
Don't spend the accent on anything but the primary action's fill, the skip link, the mark and the stage's indicator light: no accent underlines, dots, focus rings, progress bars or secondary buttons.
Don't use amber as an accent or give a warning a solid fill.
Don't bring back warm darks or cream lettering, and don't lay plain black over a painting where text sits.
Don't put the app in a device frame (laptop, monitor, browser chrome).
Don't use a painting as a small decorative tile; a painting is a whole surface or it is absent.
Don't put more than one sharp window on the deck, and don't put the deck's windows in the tab order.
Don't set uppercase, letter-spaced labels; the wordmark is the only one.
Don't box the ruled cards and steps, and don't put shadows on flat content.
